notes.md: - **Interim capital buildings:** the interim **Secretariat** and **Legislature** buildings stand at **Velagapudi** (Thullur mandal, Amaravati capital region); the Legislature building was inaugurated by CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** on **2 March 2017**.
- **Official Languages Act, 1963:** let **English** continue with **Hindi** for Union official purposes after the 15-year period ended in **1965**; amended in **1967**.
- **Yerukala:** traditional **basket makers** (bamboo and wild date palm spines); also known for fortune-telling.

new.s: To which cities were many of the Amaravati relics taken?

new.s: To which phase of Buddhism does Bojjannakonda, known for its monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra, belong?
new.x: Bojjannakonda has a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra and belongs to the Mahayana-Vajrayana phase.

new.s: Which museum in Hyderabad was formerly called the AP State Museum?

new.s: In which village of the Amaravati capital region are the interim Andhra Pradesh Secretariat and Legislature buildings located?

new.s: In which year did Arunachal Pradesh (formerly NEFA) become a full-fledged State?
new.x: NEFA became the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh in 1972 and a State in 1987.

new.s: In which year was the AP Open University, the first open university in India, set up?
new.x: The AP Open University (now Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University) was set up in 1982.
new.angle: U0272 notes gap: AP Open University 1982

new.s: In which year was the NTR University of Health Sciences, the first health university in India, set up?
new.x: The NTR University of Health Sciences, India's first health university, was set up in 1986.

new.s: Under which Chief Minister was the Janmabhoomi programme launched in Andhra Pradesh in 1997?

new.s: Which Act allowed English to continue along with Hindi for the official purposes of the Union after the 15-year period ended in 1965?

new.angle: U0272 web fact: official language debate - Official Languages Act 1963

new.s: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are there in India?
new.x: India has 75 PVTGs; undivided AP had 12, second only to Odisha (13).
new.angle: U0273 notes gap: PVTGs in India - 75

new.s: Which tribal community of Andhra Pradesh is traditionally known for basket making?
new.x: The Yerukala are traditional basket makers, weaving baskets from bamboo and wild date palm spines.

new.s: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
new.x: Lord Canning was the first Viceroy (1858) and Lord Mountbatten the last.

new.s: Who was the last Governor-General of Bengal and the first Governor-General of India?
new.x: Under the Charter Act of 1833, William Bentinck, the last Governor-General of Bengal, became the first Governor-General of India.

new.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, from which province was Orissa separated?

new.s: Who were the Secretary of State for India and the Viceroy, respectively, at the time of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
new.x: Edwin Montagu was Secretary of State and Lord Chelmsford was Viceroy; their 1918 report led to the 1919 Act.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1909:

2. It allowed a non-official majority in the provincial councils.

new.x: The 1909 Act kept an official majority at the Centre but allowed a non-official majority in the provinces.

new.s: Which Act separated the central and provincial budgets for the first time?
new.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 separated the central and provincial budgets and defined Central and Provincial lists.

new.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, how many of the six members of the Viceroy's Executive Council were to be Indians?
new.x: The 1919 Act required three of the six members of the Viceroy's Executive Council to be Indians.
new.angle: U0274 notes gap: 1919 - 3 of 6 Indians in Exec Council

new.s: Into which three lists did the Government of India Act, 1935 divide powers?
new.x: The 1935 Act made Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists, with residuary powers with the Governor-General.
new.angle: U0274 notes gap: 1935 - three lists

new.s: Which of the following Public Service Commissions was NOT provided under the Government of India Act, 1935?
new.x: The 1935 Act provided for a Federal PSC, Provincial PSCs and Joint PSCs for two or more provinces.
new.angle: U0274 notes gap: 1935 - Federal, Provincial and Joint PSCs

new.s: Which Charter Act first asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's territories in India?
new.x: The Charter Act of 1813 asserted Crown sovereignty over the Company's territories, besides ending its monopoly except tea and China trade.
new.angle: U0274 notes gap: 1813 - Crown sovereignty asserted

new.s: On which date was the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly?
new.x: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946; it was adopted on 22 January 1947.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Objectives Resolution moved 13 Dec 1946

new.s: Which part of the Constitution of India is based on the Objectives Resolution adopted on 22 January 1947?
new.x: The Objectives Resolution, adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947, became the basis of the Preamble.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Objectives Resolution -> basis of Preamble

new.s: On which date did the Constituent Assembly first meet as the Dominion Legislature, with G.V. Mavalankar as Speaker?
new.x: The Assembly first met as the Dominion Legislature on 17 November 1947, with Mavalankar as Speaker.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Dominion Legislature 17 Nov 1947

new.s: Hindi Diwas (14 September) marks the adoption of which of the following in the Constituent Assembly in 1949?
new.x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula on official language was adopted on 14 September 1949, now observed as Hindi Diwas.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Munshi-Ayyangar 14 Sep 1949 - Hindi Diwas

new.s: Where was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly held on 9 December 1946?
o: Constitution Hall (now Central Hall), New Delhi
new.x: The first meeting was held in the Constitution Hall, now the Central Hall of Parliament, New Delhi.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: first meeting venue - Constitution Hall

new.s: How many Articles, Parts and Schedules did the Constitution of India have when it was adopted?
new.x: The original Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: original Constitution 395/22/8

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Draft Constitution contained 315 Articles.
2. The original Constitution of India had 12 Schedules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Draft had 315 Articles; the original Constitution had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules (12 Schedules is today's number).
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: original Constitution - Schedules

new.s: Out of the 389 seats planned for the Constituent Assembly, how many were allotted to British India?
new.x: British India got 296 seats (292 Governor's provinces + 4 Chief Commissioners' provinces); the princely states got 93.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: 296 seats for British India

new.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, seats in the Constituent Assembly were allotted in what ratio to population?
new.x: Seats were allotted roughly one member per 10 lakh (one million) population.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: seat ratio 1 per 10 lakh

new.s: In how many sessions did the Constituent Assembly complete the framing of the Constitution?
new.x: The Assembly framed the Constitution in 11 sessions over 165 sitting days; the 24 January 1950 meeting made 12 in all.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: 11 sessions

new.s: Who was the ex-officio President of the Executive Council in the Interim Government of 1946?
new.x: The Viceroy was ex-officio President of the Executive Council; Nehru was its Vice-President.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Interim Govt - Viceroy President

new.s: When did the Muslim League join the Interim Government formed in 1946?
new.x: The Interim Government took charge on 2 September 1946; the Muslim League joined it in October 1946.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: League joined Oct 1946

new.s: Which portfolio did Jawaharlal Nehru hold in the Interim Government of 1946?
new.x: Nehru held External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations and was Vice-President of the Executive Council.
new.angle: U0275 notes gap: Nehru - External Affairs

new.s: Which portfolio did C. Rajagopalachari hold in the Interim Government of 1946?

new.s: Whose vacated seat from Bombay did Dr B.R. Ambedkar fill when he re-entered the Constituent Assembly?

new.s: Who led the work of illustrating the original Constitution of India?

new.s: How many members did the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly have?
new.x: The Drafting Committee, set up on 29 August 1947 under Ambedkar, had seven members.

new.s: Who chaired the House Committee of the Constituent Assembly?

new.s: Until when did the Provisional Parliament function before the first Lok Sabha?

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States'?
